docs.transformable.component: `Transformable` is a node's own pose: where it sits, how it is turned, how big it shows and
how high it stands. It works on a bare node and needs no box — a node can be somewhere
without occupying anything, and the desk is exactly that.
```ts
import { node, Transformable } from "game-kit"
const card = node("card", Transformable({ at: { x: 2, y: 0 }, z: 1, angle: 15 }))
## Fields
- `at` — a position in units, relative to the owner. It belongs to this node alone; inside a
container the layout decides it instead.
- `z` — height. It adds up along the chain of owners, so lifting a stack lifts everything in
it. A child can add to its owner's `z` but cannot cancel it, which is what you expect from
picking up a pack of cards.
- `angle` — a turn, in degrees, clockwise on screen. It adds up the same way `z` does: turn a
hand and everything in it turns with it, and a child cannot un-turn its owner. Only around
the screen axis — a flip has a resulting FACE, which is a different field on a different
atom.
- `scale` — size, as a multiplier. It MULTIPLIES along the chain: a half-size hand holding a
half-size card shows it at a quarter, and no sum says that. One number, not two — a
non-uniform scale is the only transform that destroys a shape's geometry, so squashing
belongs to the picture, not to the pose.
## The order inside a pose
One node's pose applies as scale, then turn, then move. Any other order turns "twice as big"
into "twice as far away" — and the two are told apart only by looking, which is how it stays
wrong for a week. Along the chain the child's pose applies first, then the owner's: a card in
a turned hand turns about the hand, never about the middle of the desk.
## `z` and the thickness of a stack
A card inside a resting stack does not stand higher than the stack — its thickness is an `at`
offset, not `z`. Layouts can only produce positions: `place()` returns points, and a point has
no `z` to write, so "a layout cannot change height" holds by construction rather than by
convention.
## Notes
- Nothing resolved is stored on the node or sent over the wire. The pose is read when the
frame is drawn, so a node that changes owner mid-animation gets the new answer immediately.
- Two nodes with the same `z` keep tree order: the later sibling is painted on top.
- A full lap changes nothing: `angle: 450` shows exactly as `angle: 90`, and a negative turn
is the same turn taken the other way round.

docs.transformable.lifted: Two overlapping plates, one lifted. The higher `z` is painted last, and the lift is the only
difference between them — same box, same kind of surface. Take `z` to −1 and the same plate
goes under; at `0` the two are equal and tree order stands, so the later sibling wins.
The container uses the `free` layout, so each plate keeps the `at` it was given. Under `row`
they would be pulled apart and there would be nothing to overlap.

turn with it — the silent one said nothing about angle and turns anyway, because `angle` adds
up and a child cannot un-turn its owner. The other card adds its own fifteen on top: what it
shows is the sum, never a replacement.

docs.transformable.sized: The one field that multiplies. The etalon on the left never scales; the hand on the right
holds a card, and both carry their own `scale`. At `0.5 × 0.5` the card shows at a quarter of
the etalon — no sum says that, which is why `multiplies` is a class of its own and why the
neutral value is one: a node that says nothing about scale changes nothing.
Take either scale to zero and the picture honestly vanishes — nothing has a size — and comes
back the moment the zero does not stand.
